title: Japan-Style Jarring Japanese Dried White Beans Dal
description: A nutty, shattering, and comforting Japanese dish made with dried white beans, dashi-extract, and a medley of spices. Perfect for a sick-day remedy or a low-fat-friendly meal option.
instructions: In a large saucepan, combine dried white beans and water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 30 minutes.
While the beans are cooking, heat sesame oil in a small pan over medium heat.
Add chopped onion to the pan and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic to the pan and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in dashi-extract, soy sauce, and sugar. Cook for an additional 2 minutes.
Once the beans are tender, drain and add them to the pan with the onion and garlic mixture.
Simmer the mixture over low heat for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt to taste, then serve hot over a talavera plate.
Garnish with chopped scallions, if desired.
